cause_quote: The new cleanup registered the system temp directory only through `targets.push({ root: os.tmpdir(), kind: "coverage", isLive: () => false });`, so ordinary agent validation output there was outside the 24-hour sweep.
user_saw: Operators could find large agent validation directories left in host `/tmp`, consuming memory and swap on tmpfs hosts until manually removed.
summary: The fix routes local agent commands into workspace-owned scratch by default and extends cleanup inventory and custody to cover those directories.
reasoning: I checked the cleanup introduction and its parent, where core exec already inherited the host environment. The new 24-hour cleanup swept `.openclaw/tmp` in registered checkouts and `node-coverage-*` in system temp, leaving default agent command output outside its scope from day one. The original documentation named those limited roots, so the defect is a missing handoff in the initial cleanup feature.
